ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human reviewer (RydeHELP safety queue) with the full chat record F3–F5, the driver statement F6 and both profiles F7/F8; note that the F6 claim of a rider opening a moving door has no gps/timeline corroboration (F1, F2 show an ordinary trip). No fare or account action should be taken against the driver without that review.
ruling.escalation_reason: Complaint is a safety incident (threat of confinement). Contemporaneous chat F3/F4 records the rider asking to get out and the driver replying "Sit down or I lock the doors."; the driver's benign account exists only in the uncorroborated post-trip statement F6. SAFE-1 requires human review of an intimidation allegation before any ruling.

rejected_claims.reason: The characterisation of F4 as a mere safety instruction rests on F6, the driver's own post-trip statement, which cannot displace the contemporaneous message F4 sent one minute after the rider's F3 request to get out; the words are read on their face under SAFE-1. [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1]

Denies intimidation, but SAFE-1 expressly covers threats and intimidation, and F5 confirms the record is complete so the conditional reference to locking the doors can be read in context against F3. [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]

The premise that the rider was opening a moving door exists only in the driver's statement F6, with no gps or timeline corroboration in F1/F2; the driver's post-trip account is a claim, not a record. [F4][F6][F1][F2][SAFE-1]

A clean profile is not a basis for refusing safety review: F8 is a profile fact and cannot decide the safety question, and SAFE-1 requires escalation of the F4 allegation to a human regardless of rating or dispute history. [F4][F8][SAFE-1]

Its core is accepted as a basis for escalation under SAFE-1, but the added SAFE-2 element (accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation) is not supported by any fact in the file: F1/F2 show an ordinary trip and no dangerous-driving allegation appears in the record. [F1][F2][SAFE-1]

Accepted as a factual statement about the rider's record, but it cannot decide the case: a clean profile is a profile fact and is not evidence that the message F4 was or was not a threat. [F7][SAFE-1]
Correct that no fare refund arises, but it is immaterial to the disposition: the case is a safety escalation, so no amount is computed and FARE-1's refund branch is not engaged. [F1][FARE-1]
